spacr.cpg_cropped:
Read the Cell Painting Gallery's cropped-site layout as OPS input (item 919, alpha).

PERISCOPE (Ramezani et al. 2025, cpg0021) publishes the pixels its
CellProfiler analysis read as one TIFF per channel and site::

    images_corrected_cropped/<plate>_Well<N>/<Channel>/<Channel>_Site_<S>.tiff

Painting channels are named after the stain (``CorrDNA``, ``CorrER``,
``CorrMito``, ``CorrPhalloidin``, ``CorrWGA``); sequencing channels are
``Cycle<CC>_<base>`` for each cycle and base, plus ``Cycle01_DAPI``. The
painting and sequencing crops of a site share one pixel grid and are already
illumination-corrected and aligned, so this reader stacks them as they are:
no stitching, no cycle registration, no rescaling.

The channel and base order is never taken from the folder listing. It is
pinned in the settings (``cpg_phenotype_channels``, ``cpg_sbs_bases``,
``cpg_sbs_dapi``) and written to the run folder, so a rerun from the saved
settings stacks the same planes in the same order.

Typical use::

    from spacr.cpg_cropped import cpg_cropped_index, load_cpg_site

    index = cpg_cropped_index(".../images_corrected_cropped/CP186A_Well1")
    site = load_cpg_site(index, "CP186A", "Well1", 45)
    site["phenotype"].shape     # (5500, 5500, 5), uint16
    site["sbs"].shape           # (12, 5500, 5500, 4), uint16
spacr.cpg_cropped.array_md5:
The md5 of an array's bytes in C order.

:param array: any array.
:returns: the hex digest.
spacr.cpg_cropped.check_cpg_complete:
Refuse an incomplete well, or drop its incomplete sites when asked.

:param index: from :func:`cpg_cropped_index`.
:param channels: from :func:`expected_channels`.
:param missing: ``'error'`` raises naming every missing file;
    ``'skip_site'`` drops each incomplete site and lists it.
:returns: ``index`` (only complete sites, every file of them), ``missing`` (the table of
    :func:`cpg_missing_files`) and ``skipped`` (``[(plate, well, site)]``).
:raises ValueError: for an unknown ``missing`` or, with ``'error'``, a
    missing file.
spacr.cpg_cropped.cpg_cropped_index:
Index a cropped-site tree from its paths, one row per file.

:param root: ``images_corrected_cropped/`` or one ``<plate>_Well<N>/``.
:param wells: keep only these wells, as ``Well1``, ``W1`` or
    ``CP186A_Well1``; None keeps all.
:param sites: keep only these sites (:func:`parse_sites`).
:param md5: add an ``md5`` column of each file's bytes.
:param headers: read each TIFF's header for ``shape`` and ``dtype``. No
    pixels are decoded either way; False leaves both empty.
:returns: the index (:data:`INDEX_COLUMNS`, plus ``md5``), sorted by
    plate, well, site, modality (phenotype first), cycle and channel.
    ``modality`` is ``phenotype`` or ``sbs``; ``cycle`` is 0 for a
    painting channel; ``base`` is the letter of a sequencing channel,
    ``DAPI`` for its nuclear channel, and empty for a painting channel.
:raises ValueError: for a well folder without ``_Well<N>``, a file whose
    name does not match its channel folder, or a tree with no site files.
spacr.cpg_cropped.cpg_missing_files:
The (site, channel) files a well lacks.

A site counts as present when any of its channels is; each present site
must then hold every channel in ``channels``.

:param index: from :func:`cpg_cropped_index`.
:param channels: from :func:`expected_channels`.
:returns: one row per missing file: ``plate``, ``well``, ``site``,
    ``channel`` and the ``expected`` file name.
spacr.cpg_cropped.cpg_settings:
The pinned reader settings, with defaults filled in.

:param settings: the OPS settings; read for ``cpg_root``, ``cpg_wells``,
    ``cpg_sites``, ``cpg_phenotype_channels``, ``cpg_sbs_cycles``,
    ``cpg_sbs_bases``, ``cpg_sbs_dapi``, ``cpg_sbs_resample``,
    ``cpg_missing`` and ``cpg_md5``.
:returns: the same keys, normalised (lists of names, ints, lower-case
    choices).
:raises ValueError: when ``cpg_root`` is empty.
spacr.cpg_cropped.cpg_site_index:
Index, check and pin a cropped-site run's input.

:param settings: the OPS settings (:func:`cpg_settings`).
:param md5: overrides ``cpg_md5``.
:returns: ``index`` (the complete sites), ``missing``,
    ``skipped``, ``channels`` (every expected channel, in order) and
    ``pinned`` (:func:`cpg_settings`).
spacr.cpg_cropped.expected_channels:
Every channel folder a complete site has, in stacking order.

:param phenotype_channels: the painting channels.
:param sbs_cycles: how many sequencing cycles; 0 for none.
:param sbs_bases: the base letters of each cycle.
:param sbs_dapi: the sequencing nuclear channel, or None.
:returns: the painting channels, ``Cycle<CC>_<base>`` for every cycle
    and base, then the nuclear channel.
spacr.cpg_cropped.file_md5:
The md5 of a file's bytes.

:param path: the file.
:param chunk: bytes read at a time.
:returns: the hex digest.
spacr.cpg_cropped.load_cpg_site:
One site's painting field and sequencing stack, exactly as stored.

Each plane is ``tifffile.imread`` of its file, unchanged: same dtype, no
rescaling, no registration.

:param index: from :func:`cpg_cropped_index`.
:param plate: the plate, for example ``CP186A``.
:param well: ``Well1`` or ``W1``.
:param site: the site number.
:param phenotype_channels: painting channels, in stacking order.
:param sbs_cycles: sequencing cycles to stack, 1 to this.
:param sbs_bases: the base of each of the four planes per cycle, in order.
:param sbs_dapi: the sequencing nuclear channel, or None.
:param resample: what to do when a sequencing plane's grid differs from
    the painting grid: ``'none'`` refuses; ``'nearest'`` or ``'linear'``
    resizes it onto the painting grid and records the factor.
:param parts: which of ``'phenotype'`` and ``'sbs'`` to read.
:returns: ``phenotype`` ``(Y, X, C)``, ``sbs`` ``(cycles, Y, X, bases)``,
    ``dapi`` ``(Y, X)`` (each None when not read), ``channels``,
    ``sbs_channels`` (``[cycle][base]`` names), ``resample_factor``
    (``(fy, fx)`` from sequencing to painting grid, ``(1.0, 1.0)`` when
    they agree) and ``paths``.
:raises ValueError: for a missing channel, planes of one modality that
    differ in shape, a grid mismatch with ``resample='none'``, or an
    unknown ``resample``.

One site's ``merged/phenotype/<plate>/<well_id>/<site>.npz``.

spacr.cpg_cropped.parse_sites:
The sites a ``cpg_sites`` setting names, or None for every site.

:param value: None or empty for all; an int; a list of ints; or a string

:returns: the sorted site numbers, or None.
:raises ValueError: for a part that is not a number or a range.
spacr.cpg_cropped.parse_well_folder:
Split a ``<plate>_Well<N>`` folder name.

:param name: the folder's base name, for example ``CP186A_Well1``.
:returns: ``plate`` (``CP186A``), ``well`` (``Well1``), ``well_id``
    (``W1``, the form spaCR tables use) and ``number`` (1).
:raises ValueError: when the name has no ``_Well<N>`` ending.
spacr.cpg_cropped.run_cpg_phases:
Index a cropped-site tree and write its sites to ``merged/`` (item 919).

``cpg_index`` builds the index from the paths, checks every site has every
pinned channel and cycle, and writes ``<dst_root>/cpg_index.csv`` (one row
per file, with ``md5`` when ``cpg_md5`` is on) and
``<dst_root>/cpg_channels.json`` (the pinned channel and base order and
every other reader setting). ``cpg_merged`` writes each complete site's
painting channels, stacked in the pinned order and exactly as stored, to
``<dst_root>/merged/phenotype/<plate>/<well_id>/<site>.npz`` (``channels``
as ``(C, Y, X)`` and a JSON ``meta`` with each plane's md5); masks are
added by the segmentation items. A site whose file exists is not redone.
The sequencing stack is not copied: the decode reads it from the index.

:param settings: the OPS settings: ``dst_root`` (required), the
    ``cpg_*`` reader settings (:func:`cpg_settings`) and ``n_workers``.
:param phases: ``"cpg_index"``, ``"cpg_merged"`` or both.
:param report: called with progress lines.
:returns: ``{"index": path, "channels_record": path, "files", "sites",
    "skipped", "merged": {...}}``.
:raises ValueError: without ``dst_root``, for an incomplete well under
    ``cpg_missing='error'``, or for an unknown phase.
spacr.ops_decode.best_overlaps:
Each first-image object's reference object of largest overlap.

Ties are broken by the higher IoU, then the lower reference label, so
the result does not depend on pixel order.

:param pairs: the ``pairs`` of :func:`label_contingency`.
:returns: one row per ``label_a`` with its chosen ``label_b``,
    ``overlap`` and ``iou``.
spacr.ops_decode.call_concordance:
Per quality class, how many matched cells fall in each concordance category.

:param pairs: one row per one-to-one matched cell pair with
    ``spacr_guide``, ``spacr_gene``, ``reference_guide``,
    ``reference_gene`` and ``quality``.
:param control: the label of this table's rows (``observed`` or
    ``shuffled_seed<k>``).
:returns: ``control``, ``quality`` (each class and ``all``),
    ``category``, ``n``, ``pct`` of the class's pairs and, on the
    ``both_called`` rows, the share with the same guide.
spacr.ops_decode.cell_calls_from_reads:
One call per cell from a per-read table: the barcode with most reads.

Feldman et al. 2019 deposit reads, not cells; the rule pinned here is
the top barcode by read count, and a tie for the top is no call.

:param reads: one row per read with the key, cell and barcode columns.
:param cell: the cell column; 0 or empty is a read outside any cell.
:param barcode: the barcode column.
:param keys: the columns that, with ``cell``, name one cell.
:returns: per cell the keys, ``cell``, ``barcode`` (None on a tie),
    ``reads`` of the top barcode and ``total_reads``.
spacr.ops_decode.centroid_matches:
Each first-image object's nearest reference centroid within a distance.

The centroid mode of the compare_calls phase, applied to the same two
label images, as the control for the mask-overlap matching.

:param first: spaCR's label image.
:param second: the reference label image.
:param max_px: the largest centroid distance of a match.
:returns: ``spacr_id``, ``centroid_reference_id`` (0 when none) and
    ``distance_px`` per spaCR object.
spacr.ops_decode.concordance_category:
The concordance category of one matched cell pair.

:param spacr_guide: spaCR's guide call or None.
:param spacr_gene: spaCR's gene or None.
:param ref_guide: the reference's guide call or None.
:param ref_gene: the reference's gene or None.
:returns: one of :data:`CONCORDANCE_CATEGORIES`.
spacr.ops_decode.edge_labels:
The labels of a label image that touch its border.

:param labels: a 2-D label image, 0 for background.
:returns: the sorted labels on the first or last row or column.
spacr.ops_decode.label_contingency:
Pixel overlap of every pair of objects of two label images, in one pass.

:param first: a 2-D label image (spaCR), 0 for background.
:param second: a label image of the same shape (the reference).
:returns: ``(pairs, area_first, area_second)``: ``pairs`` has
    ``label_a``, ``label_b``, ``overlap`` (pixels both cover) and
    ``iou`` for every pair that shares a pixel, sorted by ``label_a``
    then ``label_b``; the areas are Series indexed by label.
:raises ValueError: when the shapes differ.
spacr.ops_decode.match_masks:
Match two segmentations of one field object by object.

:param first: spaCR's label image.
:param second: the reference label image, same shape.
:param iou: the IoU a one-to-one match needs, for F1.
:param edge_policy: ``"exclude"`` leaves objects that touch the image
    border in either image out of the counts (they are counted
    separately); ``"keep"`` counts them.
:returns: ``{"matches", "counts"}``. ``matches`` has one row per spaCR
    object: ``spacr_id``, ``reference_id`` (largest overlap, 0 when
    none), ``overlap_px``, ``iou``, ``matched`` (in the one-to-one
    matching), ``matched_reference_id`` (its one-to-one partner, 0 when
    none), ``spacr_edge`` and ``reference_edge``. ``counts`` holds
    ``n_spacr``, ``n_reference``, ``tp``, ``fp``, ``fn``, ``f1``,
    ``median_iou`` (of the one-to-one matches), ``edge_spacr`` and
    ``edge_reference``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown edge policy or differing shapes.
spacr.ops_decode.one_to_one:
Optimal one-to-one matching on IoU of the pairs at or above a threshold.

The standard instance-segmentation pairing: a Hungarian assignment
maximising summed IoU over the candidate pairs, which at a threshold
above 0.5 equals keeping every candidate (two objects cannot both
overlap a third by more than half).

:param pairs: rows with ``label_a``, ``label_b`` and ``iou``.
:param threshold: the smallest IoU a match may have.
:returns: the matched rows, sorted by ``label_a``.
spacr.ops_decode.parse_site_key:
Split a ``<plate>-<well>-<site>`` key such as ``CP186A-Well3-75``.

:param text: the key; the plate may itself contain hyphens.
:returns: ``(plate, well, site)``.
:raises ValueError: when the key has fewer than three parts or the
    site is not a whole number.
spacr.ops_decode.reference_cell_calls:
A reference pipeline's per-cell calls keyed by plate, well, site and object.

:param table: the reference call table, one row per called cell.
:param columns: the column map with ``site`` (a ``<plate>-<well>-
    <site>`` key, or the site number when ``plate`` and ``well`` are
    mapped too), ``object``, ``barcode``, ``gene`` and optionally
    ``quality``, ``plate`` and ``well``; :data:`PERISCOPE_CALL_COLUMNS`
    when None.
:returns: ``plate``, ``well``, ``site``, ``object``, ``barcode``,
    ``gene`` and ``quality`` (``"all"`` when not mapped); an empty
    barcode is no call.
:raises ValueError: when a mapped column is missing.
spacr.ops_decode.run_compare_masks:
The compare_calls phase in mask-overlap mode (item 922).

spaCR's label masks and a reference pipeline's are matched object by
object on each field (:func:`match_masks`); the reference's per-cell
calls are carried to spaCR's cells through the matches and compared
with spaCR's (:func:`call_concordance`), next to two controls: the
reference calls shuffled among the cells of each site, and centroid
matching of the same cells (:func:`centroid_matches`).

:param settings: read for ``plate``, ``dst_root``,
    ``ops_compare_reference_masks`` (a path template with ``{plate}``,
    ``{well}``, ``{site}`` or ``{tile}`` and ``{object}``),
    ``ops_compare_spacr_masks`` (the same; ``.npz`` files are spaCR
    phenotype masks; default
    ``{dst_root}/{well}/phenotype_masks/site-{site}.npz``),
    ``ops_compare_reference_objects``, ``ops_compare_iou``,
    ``ops_compare_edge_policy``, ``ops_compare_mask_scale``,
    ``ops_compare_reference_calls``, ``ops_compare_call_columns``,
    ``ops_compare_spacr_calls`` (a spaCR cell table with well, site,
    label and sgRNA, or ``"reference"`` for the self-match control),
    ``ops_compare_control_seed``, ``ops_compare_match_px`` and
    ``ops_compare_fields``.
:param report: called with progress lines.
:returns: the summary, with the paths written under
    ``<dst_root>/results/ops_compare``: ``match_cells.parquet``,
    ``mask_agreement.csv``, ``call_concordance.csv``,
    ``centroid_vs_overlap.csv``, ``reference_ids.csv`` and
    ``compare_masks.json``.
:raises ValueError: for missing settings, files or columns, or masks on
    different grids without a scale factor.
spacr.ops_decode.shuffle_calls_within_si:
Reference calls permuted among the cells of each site.

:param calls: :func:`reference_cell_calls` output.
:param seed: the :func:`numpy.random.default_rng` seed.
:returns: the same rows with ``barcode``, ``gene`` and ``quality``
    permuted within each plate, well and site.
spacr.ops_image_umap:
The ``ops_profiles`` source of Image UMAP: OPS gene maps (item 918).

:func:`spacr.core.generate_image_umap` draws per-object measurements and
clusters its 2-D embedding. For OPS gene and guide profiles that is wrong:
the clusters every benchmark scores are made in the full profile space, and
a gene is not an image. With ``umap_source='ops_profiles'`` the same entry
calls :func:`run_ops_image_umap`, which

* lays the gene rows (and optionally the guide rows) out with umap-learn, for
  display only (:func:`umap_layout`);
* clusters the full profiles: a cosine kNN or PHATE graph and Leiden through
  :mod:`spacr.ops_clusters`, or a partition read from a file
  (:func:`profile_clusters`);
* builds a hierarchy of the clusters by linkage of their centroid profiles
  (:func:`cluster_hierarchy`);
* labels clusters by enrichment against versioned gene sets, BH across all
  cluster x term pairs, with a shuffled-label control
  (:func:`enrich_clusters`);
* picks, per cluster or top-level group, the medoid gene and that gene's
  cells closest to its profile (:func:`medoid_cells`) and shows their raw
  crops at ONE display range per channel shared by every crop
  (:func:`shared_display_range`), on a ring around the map whose slots are
  assigned by angle so leader lines do not cross (:func:`layout_crop_ring`);
* records the library versions that produced the layout
  (``umap_provenance.json``), because UMAP coordinates change across
  umap-learn / pynndescent / numba versions even with the same seed, while
  clusters, hierarchy, labels and medoids do not depend on the layout.
spacr.ops_image_umap.cluster_centroids:
The mean profile of every cluster.

:param rows: profile rows.
:param labels: one cluster per row.
:returns: ``(clusters, centroids)``, clusters sorted.
spacr.ops_image_umap.cluster_hierarchy:
Linkage of cluster centroid profiles (cosine), cut at group counts.

:param rows: profile rows (controls excluded by the caller if wanted).
:param labels: one cluster per row.
:param method: :func:`scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage` method.
:param levels: numbers of top-level groups to cut at.
:returns: ``(table, linkage)``; the table has ``cluster``, ``level``
    (the group count asked for), ``parent`` (the group at that level),
    ``height`` (the linkage height at which the cluster first merges)
    and ``n_genes``.
spacr.ops_image_umap.composite:
An RGB view of a raw crop at the shared ranges.

:param crop: ``(H, W, C)`` raw crop.
:param colours: channel to a matplotlib colour.
:param ranges: channel to ``(low, high)``.
:returns: ``(H, W, 3)`` float in ``[0, 1]``.
spacr.ops_image_umap.enrich_clusters:
Enrichment of every cluster for every gene set, and each cluster's label.

The background is every clustered gene except non-targeting rows; set
members outside it are dropped. Pairs with fewer than ``min_overlap``
shared genes are not tested and enter the correction as p = 1: q-values
are Benjamini-Hochberg across ALL cluster x term pairs (every cluster
times every set with a member in the background), so filtering on
overlap does not shrink the correction.

:param genes: clustered gene names.
:param labels: one cluster per gene.
:param sets: ``source``, ``term``, ``gene`` rows.
:param test: ``'hypergeom'`` (one-sided, over-representation) or
    ``'fisher_two_sided'`` (Brieflow's benchmark test).
:param min_overlap: the fewest shared genes tested.
:param q: the q-value a label needs.
:returns: ``(table, labels)``; the table has ``cluster``, ``source``,
    ``term``, ``overlap``, ``size``, ``cluster_size``, ``p``, ``q``,
    ``label`` (True for the term drawn); ``labels`` maps a cluster to
    ``(term, q)``, or ``('unlabelled', nan)``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown test.
spacr.ops_image_umap.is_control:
True for non-targeting rows.

:param names: row names.
:returns: a boolean array.
spacr.ops_image_umap.label_sets:
The gene sets clusters are labelled with, and their versions.

:param sources: ``'CORUM'`` / ``'KEGG'`` (every group), ``'CORUM@REPORT'``
    or ``'@SELECT'`` (that half of the groups, as
    :func:`spacr.ops_reference.group_halves` splits them), ``'NAME'``
    (``NAME.tsv`` in a reference folder) or ``'NAME=path'``; a file has
    ``gene_name`` and ``group`` columns.
:param reference_dir: the reference folder(s).
:returns: ``(sets, record)``; ``sets`` has ``source``, ``term``,
    ``gene``; ``record`` maps each source to its file and md5, or to
    ``'missing'`` when no file was found (the source is then skipped and
    the legend says so).
spacr.ops_image_umap.layout_crop_ring:
Assign each group to a slot on a ring around the map by angle.

Slots are evenly spaced, slot 0 at angle 0 (east), counter-clockwise.
The assignment minimises the summed angular distance between each
group's medoid point (seen from ``centre``) and its slot (Hungarian
assignment), so leader lines keep the groups' angular order and do not
cross.

:param points: group to its medoid point ``(x, y)`` on the map.
:param centre: the map centre ``(x, y)``.
:param n_slots: slots on the ring; at least one per group.
:returns: ``{group: slot}``.
spacr.ops_image_umap.layout_stability:
How faithful the layout is, over several UMAP seeds.

:param rows: gene rows.
:param labels: their clusters.
:param settings: the UMAP keys.
:param seeds: UMAP seeds.
:param k: the neighbours compared.
:returns: one row per seed: ``trustworthiness`` (cosine, ``k``) and the
    share of each gene's ``k`` nearest neighbours that are in its own
    cluster in 2-D (``same_cluster_2d``) and in the profile space
    (``same_cluster_profile``).
spacr.ops_image_umap.library_versions:
The installed versions of :data:`PROVENANCE_PACKAGES`.

:returns: ``{package: version}``, ``None`` for one not installed.
spacr.ops_image_umap.medoid_cells:
Each group's medoid gene and that gene's cells closest to its profile.

:param groups: group id to member gene names.
:param names: profile row names.
:param rows: profile rows (the space the cell rows live in).
:param cells: the per-cell addresses, with ``cell_id`` and ``gene``.
:param cell_rows: the cells' rows, same dimensions as ``rows``.
:param n: cells per group.
:param min_cell_px: skip cells whose ``cell_px`` (or ``area``) is smaller.
:param usable: a further test per cell, such as "its crop lies inside
    the field"; cells failing it are skipped.
:returns: one row per group: ``group``, ``medoid_gene``, ``cell_ids``
    (``;``-joined), ``distances``.
:raises ValueError: when the cell rows' dimensions differ from the
    profile rows'.
spacr.ops_image_umap.medoid_gene:
The gene with the smallest summed cosine distance to the others.

:param names: the group's gene names.
:param rows: their profiles.
:returns: the medoid; ties go to the alphabetically first name.
spacr.ops_image_umap.ops_umap_settings:
The ``ops_profiles`` settings with defaults filled in.

:param settings: the caller's settings.
:returns: a new dict; UMAP keys take :data:`OPS_UMAP_LAYOUT_DEFAULTS`

spacr.ops_image_umap.profile_clusters:
Clusters of the full profiles, never of the layout.

:param names: gene names, one per row.
:param rows: the full profile rows.
:param settings: ``ops_umap_partition`` (``'file:column'``, with a

:raises ValueError: when the partition file lacks genes that are mapped.
spacr.ops_image_umap.read_cell_table:
The per-cell table: addresses and the cells' profile-space rows.

:param path: a table with ``cell_id``, ``gene``, crop address columns
    (:data:`CELL_ADDRESS_COLUMNS`) and numeric embedding columns.
:returns: ``(addresses, rows)``.
:raises ValueError: without ``cell_id`` or ``gene``.
spacr.ops_image_umap.read_crop:
One raw ``(crop_px, crop_px, C)`` crop, or None when it is cut off.

:param cell: a cell row with ``field_path`` (an ``(H, W, C)`` ``.npy``)
    and ``centroid_y`` / ``centroid_x``, or ``crop_path`` / ``png_path``
    (a crop centred on the cell, cut to ``crop_px`` around its centre).

spacr.ops_large_sites:
Segmentation of large cropped OPS sites (item 921).

PERISCOPE publishes its painting images as 100 crops per well, each
5,500 x 5,500 px x 5 channels of uint16. One site is about 300 MB raw and
more than 1 GB once Cellpose holds float32 copies, flows and probabilities,
so the OPS phenotype path, sized for 2,960 px fields, cannot segment it in
one piece on a worker with a fixed RAM budget. This module adds:

* tiled segmentation (:func:`segment_tiled`): tiles of ``seg_tile_px`` with
  ``seg_tile_overlap_px`` of overlap, segmented in row-major order; copies of
  one object in two tiles are merged by IoU, keeping the copy whose centroid
  is farther from an inner tile edge (:func:`stitch_tile_labels`); a site no
  larger than one tile goes through the segmenter unchanged; each channel is
  normalised once on the whole site (:func:`normalize_site`) and the tiles
  are segmented with ``normalize=False``, so a tile sees the same values as
  the untiled site, and tiles are placed on Cellpose's own network-tile grid
  (:func:`tiling_layout`), so the network sees the same pixels tiled and
  untiled;
* chunked measurement (:func:`measure_chunked`): objects measured in row
  bands, each band read with a halo that holds every object whose centroid
  lies in it, so each object is measured once and whole;
* a RAM planner (:func:`plan_site_memory`) that picks the tile size and the
  worker count from ``seg_max_ram_gb`` and refuses a cap it cannot meet;
* the crop-edge policy (:func:`apply_edge_policy`): ``'exclude'``,
  ``'keep'`` or ``'own'`` (an object cut by a seam between two placed crops
  is kept by the crop holding its larger part);
* the ``cell_painting_phalloidin`` preset (:func:`segment_cell_painting_site`):
  nuclei on DNA, cells on ``[Phalloidin, DNA]``, one nucleus per cell, with
  the plate's nucleus diameter and the tiling-control site taken from
  populated sites spread over the well (:func:`survey_sites`);
* the agreement report against reference label masks (:func:`mask_agreement`).

:func:`run_large_site_segmentation` is the settings-file entry. The memory
model of the planner is an estimate; the peak memory actually used per site
is measured with :class:`spacr.resource_log.ResourceSampler` and written to
the site table, so the estimate can be checked against every run.
spacr.ops_large_sites.MemoryPlanError: The per-worker RAM cap cannot be met for this site.
spacr.ops_large_sites.apply_edge_policy:
Apply the crop-edge cell policy to one site's labels.

``'keep'`` keeps every object. ``'exclude'`` drops every object touching
the crop border. ``'own'`` resolves objects cut by a seam with a placed
neighbour crop (``neighbours`` maps a side to the neighbour's labels, the
neighbour abutting without overlap): the piece in this crop and the
pieces in the neighbour that meet it across the seam are one cell, and
the crop holding the larger part keeps it; on a tie the top or left crop
keeps it, so two crops never both keep or both drop a cell. Objects on a
side with no known neighbour are dropped, as with ``'exclude'``.

:param labels: the site's label image.
:param policy: one of :data:`EDGE_POLICIES`.
:param neighbours: for ``'own'``, side to neighbour label image.
:returns: ``(labels, counts)``; ``counts`` has ``edge_objects`` (objects
    touching the border), ``excluded`` and ``owned`` (border objects
    kept because this crop owns them).
:raises ValueError: for an unknown policy.
spacr.ops_large_sites.basic_features:
Shape and intensity features of every object in a label image.

:param labels: a label image.

:returns: one row per object: ``label``, ``area``, ``centroid_y``,

    ``perimeter``, and per channel ``<name>_mean``, ``<name>_sum``,
    ``<name>_std``; sorted by label.
spacr.ops_large_sites.estimate_nucleus_d:
The plate's nucleus diameter from a first segmentation pass.

Cellpose-SAM has no size model, so the diameter is read from nuclei

of the sample, clipped to ``bounds`` (CellProfiler's
``IdentifyPrimaryObjects`` range in PERISCOPE's pipeline).

:param nuclei: label images of the sample sites.
:param bounds: ``(low, high)`` in pixels.
:returns: the diameter in pixels; ``low`` when the sample has no nuclei.
spacr.ops_large_sites.large_site_setting:
Item 921's settings with defaults, the preset expanded and checked.

Values the caller sets win over the preset; the preset wins over the
defaults.

:param settings: the caller's settings.
:returns: a new dict.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown preset or edge policy.
spacr.ops_large_sites.list_sites:
The sites of a well folder, in numeric order where they are numbers.

:param well_dir: the well folder (see :func:`read_cropped_site`).
:param channels: the reader's channels; the first one's files are listed.

spacr.ops_large_sites.mask_agreement:
Object agreement of a label image with a reference label image.

Objects are paired when their IoU is at least ``iou`` (above 0.5 a pair
is unique). Agreement, not ground truth: the reference is another
pipeline's segmentation of the same pixels.

:param labels: spaCR's labels.
:param reference: the reference labels, same shape.
:param iou: the pairing threshold.
:param drop_edge: count only objects not touching the image border, in
    both images.
:returns: ``n_spacr``, ``n_reference``, ``matched``, ``precision``,
    ``recall``, ``f1``, ``median_iou`` (of matched pairs) and
    ``count_ratio`` (spaCR over reference).
:raises ValueError: when the shapes differ.
spacr.ops_large_sites.measure_chunked:
Measure every object once, whole, one row band at a time.

Each band holds the objects whose centroid row falls in it; it is read
with a halo reaching the top of the highest and the bottom of the lowest
of those objects, and every other object in the halo is masked out, so
an object is measured exactly once and never cut. Positions are given in
full-image coordinates.

:param labels: the site's label image.
:param image: the site's ``(H, W)`` or ``(H, W, C)`` pixels.
:param band_px: band height; 0 measures the whole image at once.
:param channel_names: passed to ``measure``.
:param measure: ``measure(labels, image, channel_names)`` returning one
    row per object with ``label``; :func:`basic_features` by default.
:returns: one row per object, sorted by label.
spacr.ops_large_sites.plan_site_memory:
Tile size and worker count that keep each worker under the cap.

One worker holds the raw site (uint16, every channel), two label images

(:data:`TILE_BYTES_PER_PIXEL`). The tile is halved from ``seg_tile_px``
down to :data:`MIN_TILE_PX` until it fits; workers are capped by
``seg_workers`` and by the machine's available memory divided by the cap.

:param shape: the site's ``(height, width)``.
:param n_channels: channels read per site.
:param settings: read for ``seg_max_ram_gb``, ``seg_tile_px``,
    ``seg_tile_overlap_px`` and ``seg_workers``.
:param available_bytes: memory the machine can give; ``None`` reads it

:returns: ``tile_px``, ``workers``, ``estimate_gb`` and ``cap_gb``.
:raises MemoryPlanError: when even the smallest tile exceeds the cap, or
    the machine cannot hold one worker.
spacr.ops_large_sites.preset_models:
The nucleus and cell Cellpose models the preset segments with.

Names go through spaCR's resolver, so the legacy names (``'nuclei'``,

Cell Painting Gallery's ``images_corrected_cropped``), or one
``<well_dir>/<site>.npy`` holding ``(H, W, C)`` in ``channels`` order.

:param well_dir: the well folder.
:param site: the site number or name.
:param channels: the channels to read, in order.

spacr.ops_large_sites.relabel_raster:
Renumber labels 1..N in raster order of each object's first pixel.

:param labels: a label image.
:returns: an int32 label image with the same objects.
spacr.ops_large_sites.run_large_site_seg:
Segment, measure and report every site of one cropped well.

Writes, under ``seg_dst``: ``labels/<site>_nuclei.npy`` and
``labels/<site>_cells.npy``, ``tables/<site>_cells.parquet`` (one row per
cell, measured by :func:`measure_chunked`), ``sites.csv`` (per site: objects,
edge counts, the agreement with ``seg_report_reference`` when given, peak
memory and seconds), ``agreement_well.csv``, ``settings.json``,
``nucleus_diameter.json`` (the diameter, whether it was fixed or
estimated, and the survey it came from) and, with
``seg_tiling_control_px``, ``tiling_control.json`` (:func:`tiling_control`
on a centred region of the control site's cell channels, sized by
:func:`control_layout`). The nucleus
diameter, when not fixed, and the tiling-control site come from
``seg_diameter_sites`` sites spread over the well, of which only those
with at least ``seg_diameter_min_objects`` nuclei count
(:func:`survey_sites`), never from one site that may be empty.

:param settings: item 921 settings; ``seg_sites_src`` (the well folder)
    and ``seg_dst`` are required.
:param models: ``(nucleus_model, cell_model)``; built by
    :func:`preset_models` when ``None``, on the card when ``seg_gpu``.
:param available_bytes: passed to :func:`plan_site_memory`.
:returns: ``plan``, ``sites`` (the site table as records), ``dst`` and
    ``nucleus_diameter`` (what ``nucleus_diameter.json`` holds).
:raises ValueError: when ``seg_sites_src`` or ``seg_dst`` is missing, or
    when no sampled site holds enough nuclei to estimate the diameter.
:raises MemoryPlanError: when the RAM cap cannot be met.
spacr.ops_large_sites.segment_cell_paint:
Nuclei and cells of one site with the ``cell_painting_phalloidin`` preset.

Nuclei are segmented on the DNA channel, cells on ``cell_channels``
(Phalloidin, then DNA), each normalised once on the whole site
(:func:`normalize_site`) and tiled by :func:`segment_tiled` on Cellpose's
network grid (nuclei only without a diameter, since a diameter resizes
each tile); then each
nucleus is paired with one cell by
:func:`spacr.ops_sample.pair_nuclei_with_cells` (cells without a nucleus
are dropped, as in the OPS phenotype path).

:param stack: the ``(H, W, C)`` site in the reader's channel order.
:param channel_names: one name per channel of ``stack``.
:param settings: item 921 settings (see :func:`large_site_settings`).
:param models: ``(nucleus_model, cell_model)``, anything with Cellpose's
    ``eval``.
:param nucleus_diameter: the plate's nucleus diameter; ``None`` uses
    ``nucleus_diameter`` from the settings, or no diameter.
:returns: ``(nuclei, cells, counts)`` with nucleus ``k`` inside cell ``k``.
:raises ValueError: when a preset channel is not in ``channel_names``.
spacr.ops_large_sites.segment_tiled:
Segment an image tile by tile and stitch the labels.

:param image: ``(H, W)`` or ``(H, W, C)``.
:param segment: maps an image of the same layout to a label image.
:param tile_px: tile side; 0, or an image no larger than one tile, calls
    ``segment`` once on the whole image and returns its output unchanged.
:param overlap_px: overlap between tiles, at least twice the largest
    expected object diameter.
:param iou: passed to :func:`stitch_tile_labels`.
:param align: place the tiles on Cellpose's network grid
    (:func:`tiling_layout`), so that objects away from the seams are the
    untiled run's objects pixel for pixel; only for a segmenter that
    does not resize the image.
:returns: an int32 label image of the image's height and width.
spacr.ops_large_sites.stitch_tile_labels:
One label image from per-tile label images.

Every object of every tile is ranked by the distance of its centroid to
the nearest inner tile edge, farthest first (ties by tile order, then
label). Objects are painted in that order onto unclaimed pixels; an
object is dropped when it overlaps an object already painted with IoU of
at least ``iou``, or when half or more of its pixels are already
claimed (a cut copy of an object seen whole in another tile). Labels are
then renumbered 1..N in raster order of each object's first pixel.

:param tiles: ``((y0, y1, x0, x1), labels)`` per tile.
:param shape: the full image ``(height, width)``.
:param iou: the overlap IoU at which two copies are one object.
:returns: an int32 label image.
spacr.ops_large_sites.tile_grid:
The tiles covering an image, in row-major order.

:param shape: ``(height, width)``.
:param tile_px: the tile side; 0 or a side covering the image gives one
    tile.
:param overlap_px: pixels shared by neighbouring tiles.
:returns: ``(y0, y1, x0, x1)`` boxes; the last tile of a row or column
    is moved back so it ends at the image edge and stays full size.
:raises ValueError: when the overlap is not smaller than the tile.
spacr.ops_large_sites.tiling_control:
Tiled against untiled segmentation of one region that fits untiled.

Objects of the untiled run that stay clear of every seam zone (the
strips that two or more tiles share) must come back with identical
pixels; objects in a seam zone are scored by their best IoU with a tiled
object. ``segment`` must not rescale intensities per call (Cellpose's
default), or every tile is scaled differently from the region; pass a
region normalised once (:func:`normalize_site`) and a segmenter run with
``normalize=False``.

:param image: the region, ``(H, W)`` or ``(H, W, C)``.
:param segment: maps an image to a label image.
:param tile_px: the tile side of the tiled run; smaller than the region.
:param overlap_px: the overlap of the tiled run.
:param iou: passed to :func:`stitch_tile_labels`.
:param align: passed to :func:`segment_tiled`.
:returns: ``objects``, ``away_from_seams``, ``away_identical``,
    ``at_seams``, ``at_seams_iou_ge_0_9``, ``at_seams_share`` (``nan``
    without seam objects), and ``tile_px``, ``overlap_px`` and
    ``aligned`` of the tiles used.
spacr.ops_prefix:
Decode sgRNA spacer prefixes read in situ (item 920, alpha).

CROP-seq style optical screens (Feldman et al. 2019; PERISCOPE, Ramezani et
al. 2025) sequence the guide's own spacer, not a separate barcode. The library
table (``Barcodes.csv``, column ``sgRNA``) is the whitelist, and only the first
N bases are read: CellProfiler's ``CallBarcodes`` used 10 cycles for A549 and
12 for HeLa although 12 were imaged. Spacers of different guides can share a
short prefix, so the whitelist is the set of UNIQUE prefixes, and prefixes
shared by guides of different genes are reported and never called.

What this module adds on top of spaCR's base calling:

* the library model (:func:`spacer_prefix_library`): prefixes after a cycle
  mask, collisions, the whitelist's minimum pairwise distance;
* matching (:func:`match_prefix_reads`): exact, then Hamming or Levenshtein
  distance up to a limit, an equally close pair is ambiguous;
* a shuffled-whitelist control (:func:`shuffled_library`);
* per-cell calls with a quality class (:func:`prefix_cell_calls`), by
  spaCR's read-count rules or by the pooled Cell Painting recipe's "simple"
  rules PERISCOPE used (:func:`recipe_simple_quality`);
* per-cycle or pooled crosstalk compensation (:func:`compensate_prefix`);
* the site decode (:func:`decode_prefix_site`) and the run phase
  (:func:`run_prefix_decode`) over the cropped-site layout of item 919.

A masked cycle is a base that was not read. It is removed from both the
library prefix and the read, so the key of a 10-cycle prefix with cycle 6
masked has nine letters.
spacr.ops_prefix.PrefixLibrary:
A spacer-prefix whitelist.

:param positions: the 1-based cycles the key is read from, in order.
:param keys: every distinct prefix key, sorted.
:param guides: ``key -> sorted guide spacers`` sharing it.
:param genes: ``key -> sorted genes`` of those guides.
:param callable_keys: ``key -> (guide, gene, level)`` for the keys that
    may be called; ``level`` is ``'guide'``, or ``'gene'`` for a key
    shared only by guides of one gene under ``'gene_level'``.
:param collisions: one row per key shared by two or more guides.
:param extended: ``key -> set of one-base-longer prefixes`` (the next
    unmasked spacer base appended), for Levenshtein matching.
:param summary: counts and the whitelist's minimum distance.
spacr.ops_prefix.classify_cell:
One cell's quality class from its matched reads.

:param counts: ``barcode -> (exact reads, corrected reads)`` of the
    reads that matched a callable barcode.
:param min_reads: exact reads a ``perfect`` cell needs.
:returns: a key of :data:`QUALITY_CLASSES`.
spacr.ops_prefix.compensate_prefix:
Undo dye crosstalk per cycle, pooled over cycles, or not at all.

The unmixing is brieflow's median transform (:mod:`spacr.ops_sbs`): each
channel's axis is the median of the spots it wins, after each channel is
divided by its median; ``'per_cycle'`` fits one 4 x 4 matrix per cycle,
``'global'`` one over every cycle's spots.

:param values: ``(reads, cycles, channels)`` intensities; a cycle with
    a NaN is left as it is.
:param mode: ``'none'``, ``'per_cycle'`` or ``'global'``.
:returns: float32 values, same shape.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown mode.
spacr.ops_prefix.decode_prefix_site:
Read, call and match one site's sequencing spots.

:param stack: ``(cycles, Y, X, bases)`` from cycle 1, as
    :func:`spacr.cpg_cropped.load_cpg_site` returns it.
:param library: the whitelist.
:param bases: the base letter of each plane, in order.
:param labels: a ``(Y, X)`` cell label image; each read takes the label
    under it (0 outside every cell). None leaves ``cell`` at 0.
:param threshold: the read score rise (:func:`detect_spots`).
:param crosstalk: :func:`compensate_prefix` mode.
:param metric: :func:`match_prefix_reads` metric.
:param max_distance: :func:`match_prefix_reads` limit.
:param control: a shuffled whitelist (:func:`shuffled_library`); adds
    ``control_status``.
:returns: one row per read: ``y``, ``x``, ``cell``, ``quality`` (the
    smallest per-cycle margin), then :func:`match_prefix_reads`'s
    columns, and ``control_status`` when a control is given.
:raises ValueError: when ``labels`` is not the stack's grid.
spacr.ops_prefix.detect_spots:
Find reads in a ``(cycles, Y, X, bases)`` stack as the tile decode does.

Each plane is Laplacian-of-Gaussian filtered (sigma 1, negative part
clipped); the read score is the per-channel standard deviation across
cycles averaged over channels (:func:`spacr.ops_sbs.estimate_read_locations`,
one channel at a time to bound memory); local maxima at least 2 px apart
whose score rises more than ``threshold`` above its 5 x 5 minimum are
kept, ``margin`` px from the border.

:param stack: ``(cycles, Y, X, bases)`` intensities.
:param threshold: the score rise a read needs (``ops_read_threshold``).
:param margin: border, in pixels, where reads are not taken.
:param sigma: the LoG width.
:returns: ``(peaks, values)``: ``(N, 2)`` int64 ``(y, x)``, strongest
    first, and ``(N, cycles, bases)`` float32 filtered intensities (the
    3 x 3 maximum at each peak).
spacr.ops_prefix.match_prefix_reads:
Match called reads to a prefix whitelist.

A read is first cut to the key's cycles (:attr:`PrefixLibrary.positions`;
reads given as keys with ``keyed=True`` are taken as they are). An exact
match is ``exact``. Otherwise the keys within ``max_distance`` are found:
one closest key is ``corrected``, two or more equally close keys are
``ambiguous``, none is ``out_of_library``. Under ``'hamming'`` a
distance is the number of differing cycles; under ``'levenshtein'`` a
single skipped or extra base also counts as one, matched against the
spacer's next base. An ``N`` (a cycle that was not measured) matches any
base and costs nothing; reads with one are matched by Hamming distance.
A unique match to a key that cannot be called (a prefix collision) is
``collision``.

:param reads: the called reads, one letter per cycle from cycle 1.
:param library: from :func:`spacer_prefix_library`.
:param metric: ``'hamming'`` or ``'levenshtein'``.
:param max_distance: the largest distance corrected; 0 is exact only.
    Levenshtein takes 0 or 1.
:param keyed: ``reads`` are already keys.
:returns: one row per read: ``read``, ``key`` (the read's key),
    ``prefix`` (the matched whitelist key, or None), ``distance`` (-1
    when unmatched), ``status`` (:data:`READ_STATUSES`), ``guide``,
    ``gene`` and ``level``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown metric, a negative distance, or
    Levenshtein beyond one.
spacr.ops_prefix.prefix_cell_calls:
Each cell's barcode, its read counts and its quality class.

:param reads: one row per read with ``keys``, ``status``, ``key``,
    ``distance``, ``prefix``, ``guide``, ``gene`` and ``level``
    (:func:`match_prefix_reads` joined to the read positions); rows
    whose ``cell`` is 0 are not in a cell.
:param min_reads: exact reads a ``perfect`` cell needs
    (``ops_quality_min_reads``) under ``'spacr'``.
:param keys: the columns naming a cell.
:param method: ``ops_prefix_quality_method``: ``'spacr'``
    (:func:`classify_cell`, classes :data:`QUALITY_CLASSES`) or
    ``'recipe_simple'`` (:func:`recipe_simple_quality` on the exact and
    corrected reads, each scored one minus its distance over the key
    length; classes :data:`RECIPE_SIMPLE_CLASSES`).
:returns: one row per cell with any read: ``keys``, ``reads``,
    ``matched`` (exact or corrected), ``exact``, ``corrected``,
    ``ambiguous``, ``collision``, ``out_of_library``, ``barcodes``
    (distinct callable barcodes), ``prefix``, ``guide``, ``gene`` and
    ``level`` of the top barcode (empty unless ``perfect`` or ``great``),
    ``top_reads``, ``top_exact``, ``top_share`` (of matched reads),
    ``second_reads``, ``has_exact_read`` and ``quality``.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown method.
spacr.ops_prefix.prefix_positions:
The 1-based cycles a prefix key is read from.

:param prefix_length: the prefix covers cycles 1 to this.
:param cycle_mask: cycles not read; removed from the key.
:param n_cycles: cycles imaged; the prefix may not run past them.
:returns: the kept cycles, in order.
:raises ValueError: for a prefix longer than the cycles imaged, a mask
    outside the prefix range, or a mask that leaves nothing.
spacr.ops_prefix.prefix_settings:
The item-920 settings, checked and with defaults filled in.

:param settings: the OPS settings: ``ops_library``,
    ``ops_library_sequence_col``, ``ops_library_gene_col``,
    ``ops_prefix_length``, ``ops_sbs_cycles``, ``ops_cycle_mask``,
    ``ops_prefix_collision``, ``ops_prefix_metric``,
    ``ops_prefix_max_distance``, ``ops_prefix_crosstalk``,
    ``ops_quality_min_reads``, ``ops_prefix_quality_method``,
    ``ops_random_barcode_control``, ``ops_control_seed``,
    ``ops_prefix_masks`` and ``ops_read_threshold``.
:returns: the normalised values under the same keys.
:raises ValueError: without a library, or for an unknown choice.
spacr.ops_prefix.read_fractions:
The share of reads in each status, and the control's match rate.

:param reads: rows of :func:`decode_prefix_site`.
:returns: ``reads``, a count and ``frac_<status>`` per status,
    ``frac_matched`` (exact or corrected), and with a control
    ``control_matched`` and ``control_frac_matched``.
spacr.ops_prefix.recipe_simple_quality:
Each cell's class under the pooled Cell Painting recipe's "simple" rules.

A port of ``simple_categorize`` from the Broad pooled Cell Painting
profiling recipe (:data:`RECIPE_SIMPLE_SOURCE`), which assigned
PERISCOPE's per-cell ``Perfect`` and ``Great`` classes. The spots of a
cell are grouped by gene and barcode, each group's mean score and
spot count are taken, and then: one barcode with a mean score of
exactly 1 is ``perfect`` and below 1 is ``great``; with several
barcodes, one barcode holding both the single highest mean score and
the single highest count is ``imperfect``, anything else is ``bad``.
Spots with a missing gene or barcode are left out, as the recipe's
group-by leaves them out.

:param spots: one row per spot inside a cell, with ``cell_cols``,
    ``barcode_col``, ``gene_col`` and ``score_col`` (1 for an exact
    match).
:param cell_cols: the columns naming a cell.
:param barcode_col: the matched barcode.
:param gene_col: the matched barcode's gene.
:param score_col: the match score.
:returns: one row per cell with a scored spot: ``cell_cols``,
    ``barcodes`` (distinct barcodes), ``barcode``, ``gene``,
    ``score_mean`` and ``score_count`` of the recipe's top barcode (the
    first with the highest mean score, in gene and barcode order),
    ``quality_index`` (1 to 4) and ``quality`` (a key of
    :data:`RECIPE_SIMPLE_CLASSES`).
spacr.ops_prefix.run_prefix_decode:
The ``prefix_decode`` phase: decode every indexed site against spacer prefixes.

Reads the cropped-site layout (item 919, ``ops_layout='cpg_cropped'``),
builds the whitelist, decodes each complete site's sequencing stack
(cycles 1 to the prefix's last cycle), takes each read's cell from
``ops_prefix_masks`` (or the site's ``merged/`` labels), calls cells and
writes, under ``<dst_root>/results/ops_prefix/``:

* ``library_prefix_collisions.csv`` and ``library_summary.json``;
* ``quality_classes.json`` (the quality method, its class definitions
  and the settings);
* ``reads_<plate>_<well_id>.parquet`` (one row per read) and
  ``cells_<plate>_<well_id>.csv`` (:func:`prefix_cell_calls`);
* ``site_summary.csv`` (per site: :func:`read_fractions`, cells with
  reads, cells with an exact read, cells per class);
* ``cells_per_guide.csv`` and ``cells_per_gene.csv`` (perfect and great
  cells).

:param settings: the OPS settings: ``dst_root``, the ``cpg_*`` reader
    settings and the item-920 settings (:func:`prefix_settings`).
:param report: called with progress lines.
:returns: the output paths, the library summary and the run's totals.
:raises ValueError: without ``dst_root`` or a library, or when the
    layout has fewer sequencing cycles than the prefix needs.
spacr.ops_prefix.shuffled_library:
The random-barcode control: every key's letters shuffled.

Each key (and its one-base extension) is permuted with one generator, so
the control has the same number of keys, the same length and the same
base composition as the whitelist; a shuffled key that lands on a real
key stays in the control.

:param library: the real whitelist.
:param seed: the generator seed (``ops_control_seed``).
:returns: a :class:`PrefixLibrary` whose keys all call ``'control'``.
spacr.ops_prefix.site_labels:
The cell label image of one site, or None.

:param template: ``ops_prefix_masks``: a path with ``{plate}``,
    ``{well}`` (``Well1``), ``{well_id}`` (``W1``), ``{well_number}`` and
    ``{site}`` fields, to a TIFF, ``.npy`` or ``.npz`` (``cells``) label
    image. None falls back to ``merged``.
:param plate: the plate.
:param well: the well folder name.
:param well_id: the normalised well id.
:param site: the site.
:param merged: a ``merged/`` site file; its ``cells`` array is used when
    it has one.
:returns: the labels, or None when neither source has them.
:raises ValueError: when the template names a file that does not exist.
spacr.ops_prefix.spacer_prefix_library:
Build the spacer-prefix whitelist of a CROP-seq library.

Each guide's key is its spacer's bases at :func:`prefix_positions`.
Identical spacers on several rows count as one guide. A key shared by
guides of different genes is ambiguous and never called. A key shared by
several guides of one gene is not called either under ``'exclude'``; under
``'gene_level'`` it is called as that gene, with the guides joined by
``|``.

:param library: a table, or the path of one (CSV, TSV, Parquet), holding
    ``sequence_col`` and ``gene_col``.
:param sequence_col: the spacer column.
:param gene_col: the gene column.
:param prefix_length: the prefix covers cycles 1 to this.
:param n_cycles: cycles imaged.
:param cycle_mask: 1-based cycles not read.
:param collision: ``'exclude'`` or ``'gene_level'``.
:returns: the :class:`PrefixLibrary`.
:raises ValueError: for a missing column, an unknown ``collision`` or a
    spacer shorter than the prefix.
spacr.ops_prefix.whitelist_min_distance:
The smallest Hamming distance between two keys, and how many pairs are at one.

:param keys: distinct keys of one length.
:returns: ``min_distance`` (1, 2, or 3 meaning three or more),
    ``min_distance_capped`` (True when 3 stands for three or more) and
    ``pairs_at_distance_1``.
spacr.ops_scoring.call_hits:
Hit genes by PERISCOPE's per-feature Mann-Whitney rule with a zero-TPM null.

A gene's score is its count of features with p below ``feature_p``, in
each compartment and in all (:func:`significant_feature_counts`). The
null is the scores of genes not expressed in the cell line; per FDR
level each score gets a threshold (:func:`null_threshold`). An
expressed gene is a WHOLE-CELL hit when its whole-profile count is
above that threshold, and a COMPARTMENT-SPECIFIC hit when it is not but
some compartment's count is above its own.

:param pvalues: gene by feature p-values, indexed by gene.
:param zero_tpm: the null genes.
:param expressed: the genes that can be hits.
:param compartments: as :func:`compartment_features`.
:param feature_p: the per-feature threshold.
:param fdr_levels: the FDR levels.
:param starts: the threshold search starts, ``{"compartment", "Sum"}``;
    :data:`PERISCOPE_NULL_START` when None.
:returns: ``{"scores", "thresholds", "null", "summary"}``: scores per
    gene with ``expressed``, ``zero_tpm`` and per level
    ``whole_cell_<pct>``, ``compartment_<pct>`` and ``hit_<pct>``; the
    thresholds per level; the null genes' scores; counts per level.
spacr.ops_scoring.compartment_features:
Which features belong to which compartment.

:param features: the feature names.
:param compartments: ``"periscope"`` (:data:`PERISCOPE_COMPARTMENTS`) or a
    ``{name: substring}`` mapping, matched in any case.
:returns: ``{compartment: features}`` in feature order; one feature may
    sit in several compartments, as in the reference.
spacr.ops_scoring.corum_within_r:
Pearson r of gene pairs within CORUM complexes, against random pairs.

The reference rule (PERISCOPE Figure 4C): a complex counts when more
than ``coverage`` of its listed subunits are scored genes; every
distinct pair of its scored members is a within-complex pair, and the
summary is the median r over the unique pairs pooled across complexes.
The background is the median over all pairs of scored genes. The
controls are the same number of random gene pairs and the same pairs
after shuffling the gene labels of the rows (both with ``seed``).

:param rows: genes by features (e.g. :func:`pca_rows`).
:param complexes: :func:`read_corum` output.
:param coverage: the share of a complex's subunits that must be scored.
:param seed: the controls' :func:`numpy.random.default_rng` seed.
:returns: ``{"summary", "complexes"}``: the summary rows (``observed``,
    ``all_pairs``, ``random_pairs``, ``shuffled_labels``) with ``median_r``
    and ``n_pairs``; one row per counted complex with its scored members,
    pairs and median r.
spacr.ops_scoring.expression_null:
The zero-TPM (null) genes and the expressed genes among the scored genes.

:param genes: the scored genes.
:param expression: a table with ``Gene`` and one column per cell line
    (DepMap log2(TPM+1); 0 is not expressed), or a mapping with
    ``zero_tpm`` and ``expressed_genes`` lists (the reference's
    ``<line>_CCLE_expression_summary.json``).
:param cell_line: the expression column, e.g. ``"A549"``.
:returns: ``(zero_tpm, expressed)``: zero-TPM genes sorted, expressed
    genes in ``genes`` order, controls left out.
:raises ValueError: when the cell line is not a column.
spacr.ops_scoring.gene_column:
The column of a table that names the gene.

:param table: a profile, guide or p-value table.
:returns: the first of :data:`GENE_COLUMNS` the table has.
:raises ValueError: when it has none of them.
spacr.ops_scoring.mann_whitney_table:
Per gene and feature, a Mann-Whitney U test of the gene's rows against the controls'.

The reference rule (PERISCOPE ``per_feature_hit_calling.ipynb``): the
unit is a guide-level profile row; each gene's rows are tested against
all non-targeting rows with :func:`scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu` (control
rows first, two-sided, default method), one test per feature.

:param guides: guide-level rows with a gene column and numeric features.
:param control: the gene name of the control rows.
:param features: the features tested; every numeric non-metadata column
    when None.
:returns: ``(u, p)``, each indexed by gene in order of first appearance,
    one column per feature; U is the control sample's statistic.
:raises ValueError: when there are no control rows.
spacr.ops_scoring.null_threshold:
PERISCOPE's score threshold from the null genes' scores at one FDR level.

From ``start`` downwards, the first count ``c`` that more than
``int(n / (100 / (100 * level)))`` null genes exceed sets the threshold
to ``c + 1``; a gene is a hit when its score is above it. This is the
reference's ``FDR_thresholds`` loop, kept exactly.

:param scores: the null (zero-TPM) genes' scores.
:param level: the FDR level, e.g. 0.05.
:param start: where the search starts (200 for a compartment, 500 for
    the whole profile in the reference).
:returns: the threshold.
:raises ValueError: when there are no null genes.
spacr.ops_scoring.overlap_with_reference:
Jaccard and recall of a published hit list, on genes with enough cells.

:param hits: the genes called here.
:param reference: the published hit genes.
:param cell_counts: cells per gene on the scored plate; no restriction
    when None.
:param min_cells: genes with fewer cells are left out of both lists.
:returns: ``hits``, ``reference``, ``shared``, ``jaccard``, ``recall``
    (of the reference), ``precision`` and ``restricted`` (whether the
    cell-count rule was applied).
spacr.ops_scoring.pca_rows:
Gene rows projected on the principal components closest to a variance share.

The reference keeps the number of components whose cumulative
explained variance is closest to ``variance``. spaCR uses the exact
(full) SVD, so the result is deterministic; the reference's
randomized solver differs from it in the fourth decimal of the median r.

:param profile: genes by features.
:param variance: the share, or None to keep the features.
:returns: genes by components (or the profile unchanged).
spacr.ops_scoring.profile_frame:
A profile table as numeric features indexed by gene, controls dropped.

:param table: one row per gene with a gene column (:data:`GENE_COLUMNS`)
    and numeric features; ``Metadata_*`` and ``n_cells`` are not features.
:returns: the targeting genes' rows, first row per gene, in file order.
spacr.ops_scoring.read_corum:
CORUM complexes as ``(name, subunits)`` from the ``humanComplexes.txt`` export.

:param path: the tab-separated CORUM file with ``ComplexName`` and
    ``subunits(Gene name)`` (members separated by ``;``).
:returns: one entry per row, members in file order.
spacr.ops_scoring.score_profile_benchmar:
CORUM within-complex r, STRING AUPRC and the zero-TPM hit rule on every input (item 923).

The same code scores every input of ``ops_scoring_inputs``: a reference
pipeline's deposited profiles and spaCR's. ``hits_mw_ztpm`` reads an
input's ``pvalues`` table (gene by feature, as deposited) or, without
one, tests its ``guides`` rows (:func:`mann_whitney_table`), then calls
hits (:func:`call_hits`); ``corum_within_r`` and ``string_auprc`` score
its ``genes`` profile on the genes ``ops_scoring_benchmark_genes``
names. What an input lacks is written to ``benchmark_scorable.csv``.

:param settings: the resolved settings: ``ops_scoring_inputs``,
    ``ops_scoring_metrics``, ``ops_scoring_corum_file``,
    ``ops_scoring_string_file``, ``ops_scoring_string_thresholds``,
    ``ops_scoring_corum_coverage``, ``ops_scoring_pca_variance``,
    ``ops_scoring_benchmark_genes``, ``ops_scoring_benchmark_seed`` and
    the ``ops_hits_*`` keys.
:param folder: the output folder.
:param report: called with progress lines.
:returns: the written files by name.
:raises ValueError: when a metric's reference file is missing.
spacr.ops_scoring.significant_feature_co:
Per gene, the number of features below the p threshold, per compartment and in all.

:param pvalues: gene by feature p-values, indexed by gene; a
    ``sig_gene_count`` row (the reference file's per-feature tally) is
    dropped.
:param compartments: as :func:`compartment_features`.
:param feature_p: a feature counts when its p is strictly below this.
:returns: one column per compartment and ``Sum``, integer counts.
spacr.ops_scoring.string_auprc:
Gene pairs ranked by cosine similarity against STRING edges, with the r-bin display.

:param rows: genes by features.
:param string: STRING links with ``protein1``, ``protein2`` (gene
    symbols) and ``combined_score`` (0-1000 or 0-1).
:param thresholds: STRING confidences; pairs at or above one are its
    positives, every other pair of scored genes a negative.
:param seed: the shuffled-label control's seed.
:returns: ``(auprc, bins)``: per threshold and control (``observed``,
    ``shuffled_labels``) the average precision, the random baseline
    (positive share) and the counts; per Pearson-r bin
    (:data:`STRING_BINS`, as the reference's Figure 4D) the STRING links
    among scored genes with their mean and median combined score.
:raises ValueError: when more than :data:`STRING_MAX_GENES` genes are given.
spacr.ops_large_sites.aligned_tiling:
A tile side and step that put every tile's network tiles on one grid.

Tiles whose sides have evenly spaced network tiles (stride ``s``) and
whose starts are multiples of ``s`` all run Cellpose's network on the
same network tiles as the untiled image would: a pixel at least
``NET_TILE_PX`` from a cut tile edge then gets bit-identical flows tiled
and untiled. Holds for Cellpose's defaults (``bsize=256``,
``tile_overlap=0.1``) and no resizing, that is no ``diameter``.

:param tile_px: the largest tile side wanted.
:param overlap_px: the smallest overlap wanted.
:returns: ``(tile, step, stride)``: the largest tile side no larger than
    ``tile_px``, a step between tile starts that is a multiple of the
    stride and leaves at least ``overlap_px`` of overlap, and the
    stride; None when no such tile exists.
spacr.ops_large_sites.control_layout:
The region and tile sides of the tiling control.

The region is the largest side no larger than ``side`` whose network
tiles fall on one grid, and the tile the smallest side on the same grid
that covers the region in two tiles per axis with at least
``overlap_px`` of overlap, so tiled and untiled runs share every network
tile away from the seams (:func:`aligned_tiling`). Without such a pair
the region is ``side`` and the tile ``(side + overlap_px) // 2 + 1``,
unaligned.

:param side: the region side asked for (``seg_tiling_control_px``).
:param overlap_px: the overlap asked for.
:returns: ``(region_px, tile_px, aligned)``.
spacr.ops_large_sites.network_tile_start:
Where Cellpose runs its network along one image axis, in image coordinates.

Cellpose pads an image to a multiple of 16 plus 8 px on each side and
spreads ``ceil((1 + 2 * overlap) * padded / bsize)`` network tiles evenly
over the padded side (``cellpose.core.run_net`` without resizing). A
pixel's flows are the tapered mean of the network tiles that cover it, so
two runs give a pixel the same flows only when the same network tiles,
with the same pixels, cover it.

:param length: the image side in pixels.
:param bsize: the network tile side.
:param overlap: Cellpose's ``tile_overlap``.
:returns: the start of each network tile; negative starts lie in the
    padding.
spacr.ops_large_sites.normalize_site:
Cellpose's percentile normalisation, computed once on a whole site.

Cellpose normalises every image it is given, so a tile is scaled by its
own 1st and 99th percentiles and the same pixel gets different values in
two tiles and in the untiled site. Here the percentiles of each channel
come from the whole site, with the arithmetic of Cellpose's
``normalize_img`` (``normalize99`` with its subsampling; a flat channel
becomes zeros), and every tile is then segmented with
``normalize=False``. A site that fits in one tile gets exactly the values
Cellpose would have computed itself.

:param image: ``(H, W)`` or ``(H, W, C)``.
:param percentiles: ``(lower, upper)``.
:returns: a float32 copy of ``image``, normalised per channel.
spacr.ops_large_sites.sample_sites:
``n`` sites spread evenly over a well's site list, first and last included.

:param sites: the well's sites in run order.
:param n: how many to take; at least one.
:returns: the sampled sites, in run order.
spacr.ops_large_sites.survey_sites:
The plate's nucleus diameter and the tiling-control site from a sample of sites.

A well's first site is often an empty corner of the well, so neither the
diameter nor the tiling control may come from it. A sampled site counts
only when it holds at least ``min_objects`` nuclei; the diameter is the
median equivalent diameter over every nucleus of those sites, clipped to
``bounds`` (:func:`estimate_nucleus_diameter`), and the control site is
the one with the median nucleus count among them (the lower of the two
middle sites when their number is even).

:param sites: the sampled sites, in run order.
:param nuclei: per site, its nuclei as a label image.
:param bounds: ``(low, high)`` in pixels.
:param min_objects: the fewest nuclei a site needs to be used.
:returns: ``diameter_px``, ``sites_sampled``, ``objects_per_site``,
    ``diameter_per_site`` (``None`` for a site without nuclei),
    ``sites_used``, ``min_objects`` and ``control_site``.
:raises ValueError: when no sampled site holds ``min_objects`` nuclei.
spacr.ops_large_sites.tiling_layout:
The tiles :func:`segment_tiled` uses for one image.

Without ``align`` these are :func:`tile_grid`'s tiles. With ``align``,
and when the image needs more than one tile, the tile side and step come
from :func:`aligned_tiling`, and each tiled side is padded at its end so
that the last tile also starts on the network grid; the stitched labels
are then cut back to the image.

:param shape: ``(height, width)``.
:param tile_px: the tile side asked for.
:param overlap_px: the overlap asked for.
:param align: put the tiles on Cellpose's network grid.
:returns: ``boxes`` (in padded coordinates), ``padded`` (the padded
    shape), ``tile_px`` and ``overlap_px`` (those used) and ``aligned``.
